titulo: Your kidneys filter ~180 L a day
caption:
Did you know your kidneys filter about 150 to 180 liters of plasma a day? Most of it goes right back into your blood.

Here is the basic path through one nephron: blood arrives through the afferent arteriole, the glomerulus filters water and small solutes under pressure (about 125 mL per minute on average), and the tubule reabsorbs about 99% of the filtrate. Only about 1 to 2 liters leave as urine.

Which step surprises you most? Tell us in the comments.

Sources: OpenStax, Anatomy & Physiology 2e, chapter 25 (The Urinary System); NIDDK, "Your Kidneys & How They Work". Educational content, not medical advice.
